headline: GitHub Copilot adds Claude agent preview and enhanced features to JetBrains IDEs
summary: The June 2026 update for GitHub Copilot in JetBrains IDEs introduces organizational agents, multi-step CLI messaging, and Claude as a public preview agent provider, enhancing team productivity.
details: The June 2026 update for GitHub Copilot in JetBrains IDEs brings significant upgrades, including core AI agent power, team-wide governance, and true multitasking. These features, available now, aim to transform AI productivity from sandboxes into integrated workflows.

Key new features include organization- and enterprise-level agents, multi-step CLI messaging, summarized debug logs, and Claude as a public preview agent provider. Improvements to the model picker and a per-turn AI credits indicator are also part of the update. Each enhancement addresses specific developer and team challenges.

Admins can now publish and curate organization-level agents within JetBrains IDEs, standardizing workflows and enforcing best practices across teams. This eliminates manual configuration and ensures new hires and contractors align with team conventions from the start.

The updated Copilot CLI session allows developers to queue, steer, or send follow-up messages while a prior agent request is still processing. This unblocks workflow, preventing wasted time previously spent waiting or canceling ongoing agent actions.

Claude, Anthropic's language model, is now available in public preview as an agent provider within JetBrains Copilot. Users can select Claude for agent turns, leveraging its strong performance in reasoning, summarization, and code assistance tasks.

This integration provides flexibility, allowing Claude to serve as the main engine or a fallback. The new model picker also gives developers direct, session-by-session control over which AI model powers their agent, enhancing transparency and customization.

A per-turn AI credits indicator now shows real-time resource consumption, offering transparency for teams tracking budgets. This level of control and cost visibility is crucial for serious development teams.

topic: google ai studio session data loss bug
headline_marked: I Copied a Google AI Studio Session by Hand. [[68% of the Data Was Gone]].
headline: I Copied a Google AI Studio Session by Hand. 68% of the Data Was Gone.
summary: Manually copying Google AI Studio (Gemini) sessions can result in an average loss of 60-70% of the data, including critical system prompts and truncated responses.
details: An experiment revealed that manually copying a Google AI Studio (Gemini) session into a text file resulted in an average data loss of 60-70% compared to the official JSON export. This significant data discrepancy means most of the session state is not preserved.

Crucial elements like the initial system prompt, which defines the model's behavior, are completely missed by manual copy. This context is vital for understanding the conversation's foundation but is not visible in the main chat pane.

Longer Gemini responses often include a "Show more" button; if not expanded before copying, these responses are cut mid-sentence. Additionally, newlines and indentation within code blocks, especially in JSON or YAML outputs, can become corrupted, making them unparseable.

The model's internal reasoning trace, stored separately from the visible conversation, is also entirely absent in manual copies. Because the visible conversation appears coherent, detecting these missing parts, particularly the system prompt, is challenging.

The official JSON export, though potentially large (200,000+ lines in one case), provides the complete and accurate session data. It is the only reliable method for preserving full conversation logs and all associated context.

Developers are advised to make regular use of the service-provided export feature to prevent irreversible data loss. Waiting too long to export can lead to more significant data gaps as sessions grow in length and complexity.
